sections.h2: What is Lamar County, Georgia known for?
sections.html:
Lamar County lies between Atlanta and Macon, and Barnesville is its seat. Barnesville was settled in 1826, and its leaders petitioned the legislature in 1869, 1906, 1912 and 1916 before the county finally came into being in 1920, cut from Monroe and Pike counties. The result is about 185 square miles of rolling land whose streams run to the Flint and Ocmulgee rivers.

The town earned the title Buggy Capital of the South. One factory predicted in 1897 that it would ship at least 1,200 buggies, and a September Buggy Days parade still shows off original Barnesville buggies. Gordon State College, founded in 1872 as Gordon Institute and a four-year school since 2007, fills out the town's profile, and the Barnesville Expo Center joins a wetlands trail to a livestock arena. Pecan and peach groves cover the farmland.

The population stood at 9,745 in 1930, reached 18,317 in 2010 and 18,500 in 2020. Land area is 183.50 square miles, and the 2020 density of 100.8 residents per square mile is the highest of the four counties in the Census comparison.

Settlement came after the 1821 treaty with the Lower Muscogee (Creek), which ceded the land of Monroe, Pike and Crawford counties and brought English settlers from Virginia, the Carolinas and older Georgia counties. Gordon Military College (1927 to 1972) trained men who served in World War II, Korea and Vietnam, and the Expo Center bills itself as the first in the nation to join wetlands to an exhibition hall.

sections.h2: How fast is Lamar County growing, and what does it mean for prices?
sections.html:
Lamar County added 13.2% to its head count after April 2020, according to the Census estimate through July 2025, far ahead of Johnson, Jones or Lanier.

The $216,500 median owner-home value tops the four counties, and the 31.8-minute commute is the longest. With 136 permits pulled in 2025, an older Lamar County house will be shopped against new construction.

sections.h2: What does the Lamar County economy add to the housing picture?
sections.html:
A homeowner with a mortgage pays a median of $1,469 a month and one without pays $526, while renters pay $878. The county has 7,133 households of 2.60 people on average, and 92.5% of residents did not move in the past year.

Employers numbered 275 in 2023, supporting 3,775 jobs (up 10.1% over 2022) and $174,423 thousand in payroll, and 1,922 nonemployer businesses were counted in 2024. Retail sales were $150,591 thousand in 2022, which works out to $7,733 per resident, and transportation and warehousing took in $20,621 thousand, almost as much as health care and social assistance at $22,229 thousand. Another $23,100 thousand came from accommodation and food service. Labor-force participation is 56.7%. Among adults 25 and over, 89.6% finished high school and 19.2% hold a bachelor's degree. Poverty is 12.6%, 1,320 residents are veterans, 21.7% of residents are under 18, and 13.5% of people under 65 lack health insurance. Foreign-born residents make up 2.7% of the county, and 93.2% of households have a computer.

sections.h2: Where do I go for Lamar County property tax questions?
sections.html:
Barnesville hosts every office a seller needs.

  • Tax Commissioner: 790 Veteran's Pkwy, Barnesville, GA 30204; mail to P.O. Box 850; phone (770) 358-5162. Walk-in hours are Monday through Thursday, 8 to 4:30, and Friday, 8 to 4:15, with a drive-thru that closes 15 minutes earlier.
  • Tax Assessor, (770) 358-5161: values, appeals and homestead forms, Monday to Thursday 8 to 5 and Friday 8 to 4.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: the deed room in the courthouse.

The commissioner's website accepts online payment of property tax and car tag renewals. The site also stresses that the commissioner neither sets values nor chooses millage, so a complaint about a high figure goes to the assessors.

sections.h2: When are Lamar County taxes due, and what happens after?
sections.html:
The county mails bills by mid-September and wants payment by November 15, a schedule that began with the 2018 tax year. It beats Georgia's December 20 default by five weeks, which surprises owners new to the county.

  • Late real estate and business personal property bills collect 1% interest per month.
  • Amounts still open 90 days after the deadline take a 10% penalty.
  • The FAQ says a lien (fifa) goes on file once taxes are over 30 days late, and credit bureaus may see it.
  • Mobile homes are due April 1; late ones pick up a 10% filing penalty and 1% monthly, and can be auctioned.

State guidance also says interest should wait 60 days after the bill's postmark, so keep the envelope. A refund request for tax paid in error must begin inside three years.

sections.h2: Which Lamar County homestead exemptions can I file for?
sections.html:
The assessors take forms from January 1 to April 1 and cannot extend the window, so a late filer loses that year. Once approved, an exemption renews itself. Carry a driver license and either your 1040 or a signed income affidavit.

  • State types carry codes: S1 regular homestead, S3 elderly at 62, L4 elderly at 65, S5 disabled veteran and SS surviving spouse of a veteran, the last two requiring VA proof of 100% service-connected disability.
  • Over 65: Lamar takes $20,000 off the county operating levy, nothing else.
  • Over 70: $7,000 comes off school operating tax and school bond tax.
  • Disabled owners: $15,000 off school operating tax when combined household income is under $20,000, documented by two physicians or a Social Security letter that declares 100% disability.

The county says you must satisfy the state rules before any local break applies. Owners 62 and up with gross household income at or below $15,000 may also defer tax. For a mobile home to count as a homestead, the home and the land under it must have the same owner.

sections.h2: How does a Lamar County owner appeal a value?
sections.html:
County appraisers lean on recent sales, measured at January 1, and the spring notice shows the result. An owner who objects has 45 days from the notice date and may argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption. The letter goes to the assessing board and picks a route, and cases that go to the Board of Equalization are heard by a panel the Grand Jury appoints.

Landowners have preferential programs. Lamar cites section 48-5-7.4 for conservation use and residential transitional land, 48-5-7.4.1 for agricultural land and 48-5-7.2 for rehabilitated historic property, and every one asks for a covenant of 10 years or more. Enrolled acreage needs a call to the assessors before the deed changes hands.

sections.h2: How do I sell a Lamar County house with taxes still owed?
sections.html:
Request a payoff that folds in interest and penalty, and check with the Clerk for a recorded fifa. The closing agent pays out of the seller's share and secures the release. January 1 ownership decides who owes the year, so most contracts prorate.

When the owner has died, the county Probate Court can explain how to open the estate before a listing goes up. Cash buyers in Barnesville or the rural parts of the county will still expect the payoff settled at closing.

faqs.q: What is the due date for Lamar County property tax?
faqs.a: November 15. Bills normally go out by September 15, and mobile homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: What do late Lamar County payments cost?
faqs.a: 1% per month interest after the due date plus a 10% penalty at 90 days. The FAQ adds that a lien can be recorded after 30 days.

faqs.q: Do older Lamar County owners get extra relief?
faqs.a: Yes. Past 65, $20,000 comes off the county operating levy, and past 70, $7,000 comes off school operating and bond tax, once the state rules are satisfied.

faqs.q: What does a typical Lamar County house cost?
faqs.a: About $216,500, the 2020-2024 Census median for owner-occupied homes. The county had an estimated 20,941 residents in July 2025.

faqs.q: Who accepts Lamar County homestead applications?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor's office, from January 1 through April 1. Bring a driver license and a 1040 or signed income affidavit.
